question.problem:
Compute $P(1<X\le 5)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}x,\, & 0\le x\le 6, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X\le 5) & ={\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{18}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{36}{x}^{2}]}_{1}^{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
